paper.title: Contextual Slate GLM Bandits with Limited Adaptivity

unmapped: Slate structure: N slots, each with its own item set X^i_t in R^d; slate is concatenation in R^{Nd}; one item chosen per slot; single scalar GLM reward per slate
Item sets for each slot drawn i.i.d. from a distribution D^i
Rewards in [0,R] almost surely with known R; link mu is L_mu-Lipschitz, self-concordant
Each item has l2 norm at most 1/sqrt(N)
Learner knows the number of slots N, the non-linearity parameter kappa (or an upper bound), failure level delta
O(log log T) batches fixed a priori
Diversity assumption (Assumption 2.1): E[x^i_t x^i_t^T | F_{t-1}] >= rho I and E[x^i_t | F_{t-1}] = 0
settings.definition_quote: The learner is required to partition the horizon $[T]$ into $M$ disjoint batches $\mathcal{T}_1 , \ldots , \mathcal{T}_M$ \emph{apriori}, and the policy of selecting slates can only be updated between two consecutive batches. ... we assume that in each slot $i \in [N]$, the set of items $\X^i_t ~\forall t \in [T]$ are sampled independently from a distribution $\mathcal{D}^i$ supported on $\R^d$.

unmapped: Slate structure: N slots with item sets X^i_t in R^d; one item per slot; single scalar GLM reward per slate
Rarely-switching limited adaptivity: learner adaptively decides when to re-estimate parameters (few policy updates)
Rewards in [0,R] a.s. with known R; link L_mu-Lipschitz, self-concordant
Learner knows N, kappa (or upper bound), delta
settings.definition_quote: Here, while the learner is constrained to estimate $\bm\theta^\star$ only $M$ times, she can adaptively decide when to make these estimates. ... We do not assume any stochasticity in the item sets, i.e., they can be adversarial.

bound.regime: T >= T_0 (Lambert-W threshold depending on rho, N, d, delta, L_mu)

symbols.R_max: almost-sure upper bound on rewards (rewards in [0,R])
symbols.N_slots: number of slots in the slate
symbols.mudot_star_avg: E over item sets of mu_dot(x_star^T theta_star), expected reward sensitivity at the optimal slate

conditions: Diversity assumption: E[x^i_t x^i_t^T|F_{t-1}] >= rho I and E[x^i_t|F_{t-1}] = 0 for all slots
T >= T_0 = delta/(2dN) exp(-2 W_{-1}(-3 rho^2 sqrt(delta) / (2 sqrt(2dN)(48 L_mu^2 + 8 L_mu N rho)(N-1)^2)))
tuning: batch lengths |T_0| = floor(sqrt T), |T_m| = floor(T^{1-2^{-m}}), M = O(log log T)
gamma = O(S R sqrt(N d log(T/delta)))

source.label: thm:regret_batch_slate_glincb
source.quote: At the end of $T$ rounds,  \batchedalgoname\ (Algorithm \ref{alg:batched_algorithm}) incurs a regret $R(T)$ which can be bounded as \[ R(T) = \tilde{\O}\left( RS N d^{3/2} \sqrt{T \cdot \E_{ \{\mathcal{X}^i \sim \mathcal{D}^i\}_{i \in [N]}}   \dot\mu(\bm{x}_{\star}^\top \bm\theta^\star)}  \right) \]

results.notes: Restated with explicit conditions as Theorem A.1. Regret defined as E[sum max_x r_t(x) - r_t(x_t)] but analysed via means mu(x*^T theta) - mu(x_t^T theta), recorded as pseudo-regret against per-round best slate. Lower-order term e^{3S} sqrt(kappa) T^{1/4} hidden in O_tilde. Per-round time poly(N).

symbols.mudot_star_avg: expected mu_dot(x_star^T theta_star) over item-set distributions (1/kappa_1)
symbols.mudot_star_max: max over item sets of mu_dot(x_star^T theta_star) (1/kappa_2)

conditions: T >= T_0 (Lambert-W threshold as in Theorem A.1)
tuning: Distributional optimal design (Ruan et al. 2021) replaces G-optimal design

source.label: thm:regret_Batch_Slate_GLinCB_distributional_optimal_design
source.quote: Let $R(T)$ denote the regret of Algorithm \ref{alg:Batch-Slate-GLinCB_with_Distributional_Optimal_Design}. If ... and $T \geq T_0$ ... then, \[ R(T) = \tilde{\O} \left( RSNd\sqrt{T}  \cdot \min\left\{ \sqrt{d \cdot \E_{\{\mathcal{X}^i \sim \mathcal{D}^i\}_{i=1}^N}   \dot\mu(\bm{x}_{\star}^\top \bm\theta^\star)} ,  \sqrt{N \cdot \max_{\{\mathcal{X}^i \sim \mathcal{D}^i\}_{i=1}^N }\dot\mu(\bm{x}_\star^\top \bm\theta^\star)} \right\}  \right).\]

results.notes: Also stated informally as Remark 3.1. Same regret-definition caveat as r1.

bound.regime: T >= T_0 (max of two Lambert-W thresholds)

source.label: thm:rs_slate_glincb_regret
source.quote: At the end of $T$ rounds, \texttt{RS-SlateGLinCB} (Algorithm \ref{alg:rarely_switching_alg}) incurs a regret $R(T)$ which can be bounded as \[ R(T) = \tilde{\O}\left( R\sqrt{T} + RS^{1/2}Nd \sqrt{\sum_{t \in [T]} \dot\mu(\bm{x}_{t,\star}^\top \theta^\star)} \right). \]

results.notes: Restated with conditions as Theorem C.1 (sum over post-warm-up rounds). Item sets may be adversarial. Regret-definition caveat as r1. Environment set to stochastic_iid since rewards are GLM-stochastic; contexts adversarial.

source.label: lemma:rs_updates
source.quote: During $T$ rounds, \texttt{RS-SlateGLinCB} (Algorithm \ref{alg:rarely_switching_alg}) updates its policy at most $\O(Nd \log T)$ times.

results.notes: Bound on the number of policy updates, not regret. Probability type not stated; determinant argument is deterministic, so 'high_probability' is uncertain.

cited_results.setting_description: Rarely-switching GLM contextual bandit applied to slates: number of policy updates (not regret)
Fully adaptive contextual logistic slate bandit under a (kappa-scaled) diversity assumption
